concerns: The study is a single-prompt, single-system, single-domain pilot (n=10 runs of one commercial DRA), and the authors explicitly disclaim generalization, so the empirical contribution is preliminary rather than a robustly validated finding.

The entity extraction and canonicalization pipeline relies on un-audited LLM-based stages (Gemini 2.5-flash and gpt-5.4-mini), with no annotation-quality audit or inter-rater validation, leaving the headline Jaccard values subject to unquantified measurement noise.

The evaluation cannot separate retrieval-side from generation-side stochasticity, and exact URL matching conflates web drift and URL-form variability with agent instability, weakening the interpretation of the citation and edge-overlap results.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the representation and questions are intriguing, testing 10 runs of a single prompt on a single black-box agent constitutes preliminary or pilot-level evidence rather than a robust, generalizable benchmark study. The dependence on unvalidated LLM extraction and deduplication without human annotation audits further introduces scientific uncertainty.

evidence.excerpt:
verifiably factually correct. The contributions presented here are threefold.
First, we propose a three-level representation of DRA outputs, i.e. canonicalized named entities, citations, and entity–
citation pairs, as an evaluation lens for self-consistency under repeated identical prompting. Second, applying this
lens to a single commercial DRA on an open-ended topical cybersecurity related prompt, we show that entity-level
agreement is substantially higher than citation-level agreement. Third, we show that pairwise agreement varies sharply
across entity classes in a way that tracks the presumed size of the underlying entity space.

evidence.excerpt:
To study the self-consistency of a deep research system under fixed user inputs, we issue an identical open-ended
cybersecurity prompt to a single commercial deep research system (Google deep-research-preview-04-2026,
accessed through the API on 2026-04-27) in 10 repeated iterations of the same prompt, shown in Figure 1. Each of the
ten runs produced a main report with links to citations. Inline citations in the raw response were emitted by the agent as
a redirect URL. These URLs are followed by an HTTP GET request with a Chrome-likeUser-Agent and the resolved
URL is recorded. These raw reports and cited sources are cleaned with a deterministic preprocessing pipeline before
extraction. Resolved citation URLs were retained as citation identifiers, but the content of cited web pages was not
included in the entity-overlap analysis.
Entities were extracted from all preprocessed documents

set; curves that remain steep indicate that each additional run keeps retrieving unseen entities.

evidence.excerpt:
Across the 10 runs, outputs contained a median of 5,292 words (range: 4,837–6,152), 199 extracted entity mentions
(162–271), 162 distinct canonical entities after deduplication (139–193), 2.96 entities per 100 words (2.42–3.64), and
79 distinct citation URLs (66–101).
Figure 2 shows the distribution of pairwise Jaccard similarities across all 45 run pairs, broken down by entity class as
well as aggregated for the overall entity set and for cited sources. Agreement between any two runs is low in absolute
terms: the overall entity Jaccard has a median of 0.12, meaning that any two reports share only about one canonical
entity in eight, despite being responses to an identical prompt. Overlap of citations is even lower, with the median
Jaccard similarity score between sets of citations in two reports being just over 0.01, indicating that repeated runs of
the same query rarely cite the same

evidence.excerpt:
Because
entity–citation edge equality depends on exact resolved URL matches, the edge results should be interpreted as URL-
level grounding stability rather than semantic evidence stability. Two different URLs may support similar claims, and
the same underlying source may sometimes be reachable through different URL forms.
Extraction and canonicalization noise.Our pipeline relies on LLM-based entity extraction and deduplication
stages. We did not conduct a full annotation-quality audit of either stage. Spot checks suggest minor inconsistencies in
granularity, for example whether versioned variants of the same model are merged into a single canonical entity or

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The study is a single-prompt, single-system, single-domain pilot (n=10 runs of one commercial DRA), and the authors explicitly disclaim generalization, so the empirical contribution is preliminary rather than a robustly validated finding.

The entity extraction and canonicalization pipeline relies on un-audited LLM-based stages (Gemini 2.5-flash and gpt-5.4-mini), with no annotation-quality audit or inter-rater validation, leaving the headline Jaccard values subject to unquantified measurement noise.

The evaluation cannot separate retrieval-side from generation-side stochasticity, and exact URL matching conflates web drift and URL-form variability with agent instability, weakening the interpretation of the citation and edge-overlap results.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No optimization loop was performed on the evaluated agent, so signal reuse is inapplicable.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Pairwise Jaccard similarity and discovery curves computed over entities extracted and deduplicated by Gemini 2.5-flash and gpt-5.4-mini, plus resolved citation URLs.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Not applicable; the commercial deep research agent was queried as a black-box service without parameter tuning or adaptation.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported findings accurately reflect the observed run metrics, such as a median pairwise entity Jaccard of 0.12 and citation Jaccard of ~0.01 [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0015, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0016]. However, the claims are inherently constrained by the single-prompt, single-model setup and exact URL matching proxy [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0022, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0024].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation is restricted to n=10 runs of a single prompt on a single commercial system in one domain [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0011, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0022]. As an empirical characterization, it offers exploratory observations about entity vs citation stability, but the extremely narrow scope limits broader scientific conclusions.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No optimization loop was performed on the evaluated agent, making signal reuse inapplicable.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Pairwise Jaccard similarity and discovery curves calculated over entities extracted and deduplicated by Gemini 2.5-flash and gpt-5.4-mini, alongside resolved citation URLs [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0012, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0013].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Not applicable; the commercial deep research agent was queried as a black-box service without parameter tuning or adaptation in this study [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0011].

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge major limitations, including reliance on a single prompt, domain, and commercial system, inability to separate retrieval from generation stochasticity, potential web drift, exact URL matching constraints, and un-audited extraction/canonicalization noise [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0022, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0024].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology queries Google deep-research-preview 10 times, followed by deterministic preprocessing, entity extraction via Gemini 2.5-flash with langextract, and three-run majority voting canonicalization via gpt-5.4-mini with openai-gabriel [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0011, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0012]. The analytical formulation using Jaccard overlap and cumulative discovery curves is clearly defined [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0013, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0014], though the extraction and deduplication stages lack formal validation or human quality auditing [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0024].
primary.quality_rationale: While the representation and questions are intriguing, testing 10 runs of a single prompt on a single black-box agent constitutes preliminary or pilot-level evidence rather than a robust, generalizable benchmark study. The dependence on unvalidated LLM extraction and deduplication without human annotation audits further introduces scientific uncertainty.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript studies the self-consistency of outputs from a commercial deep research agent across 10 repeated queries of a single cybersecurity prompt, analyzing overlap among extracted canonical entities, citation URLs, and entity-citation pairs via pairwise Jaccard similarity and discovery curves [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0004, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0010, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0011].

scholarly_quality.rationale: While the representation and questions are intriguing, testing 10 runs of a single prompt on a single black-box agent constitutes preliminary or pilot-level evidence rather than a robust, generalizable benchmark study. The dependence on unvalidated LLM extraction and deduplication without human annotation audits further introduces scientific uncertainty.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly acknowledge major limitations, including reliance on a single prompt, domain, and commercial system, inability to separate retrieval from generation stochasticity, potential web drift, exact URL matching constraints, and un-audited extraction/canonicalization noise [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0022, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0024].
